sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Oak Park
sections.html:
An Oak Park owner can hire an agent, go it alone, or sell to someone who buys houses for cash. After any of them, three offices need paperwork: the city assessor, the Municipal Services Department, and the Oakland County deed office.

Much of Oak Park was built in the postwar boom, so a house often carries decades of updates, some permitted and some not. A buyer with a mortgage orders an inspection and an appraisal. A buyer without one prices repairs into the offer. Get closing date, repair terms and your net amount in writing from each, then compare the totals.

Begin with what you control. Find your last deed, locate permit records for the roof, furnace and electrical work, and collect your utility account details.

Oak Park is a Detroit-bordering suburb about 14 miles northwest of downtown. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 29,072 residents, which is 1.7% below the 2020 base. Houses sit close together on small lots, so street-level comparables carry weight.

For 2020 to 2024 the middle owner-occupied value was $212,300, rent in the middle of the range was $1,396 a month, and owners lived in 63.3% of homes. The city counts 12,452 households with a middle income of $71,510.

The city assessor publishes a sales study each year. The 2026 assessment-year study draws on sales from April 1, 2023 through March 31, 2025, and an economic condition factor report can be looked up by parcel on BSAonline.com. Reading both shows how the assessor treats houses like yours, which helps when weighing an offer.

Oak Park Schools serves most of the city. Homes between 10 Mile and 11 Mile Roads belong to the Berkley School District, and about a square mile at the east end is in Ferndale Public Schools. Two neighbors can be in different districts, so check the exact address.

sections.h2: City charges that can come up at a sale
sections.html:
The city sets fixed charges for occupancy, rental registration and alarm permits, and some of them surface when a house changes hands.

Oak Park city charges
ChargeAmount and when it applies
Certificate of occupancy$50 for occupancy only or reissuance
Rental registration$80 for two years
Rental inspection$150, due every two years or after a change in tenancy
Emergency alarm permit$20 one time; each change in ownership of an operable alarm needs a new permit
Garage sale permit$10, required for any residential garage sale

A certificate of occupancy is needed before any new or altered building is used, and applications go to Municipal Services at 14300 Oak Park Boulevard. Rentals must pass inspection before occupancy, so a house emptied between tenants may need one before anyone moves back in.

sections.h2: Permits a seller should be able to show
sections.html:
The city issues separate building, electrical and demolition permits, and the Building Division at 14300 Oak Park Boulevard takes building applications. Its Roofing Guidelines for Residential Properties describe the roofing permit and the inspections a roof job requires.

If a prior owner did the roof, wiring or an addition, ask Municipal Services what is on record for your address. A missing final sign-off is cheaper to resolve before listing than after a buyer's inspector spots it. City code also asks owners, occupants and tenants to maintain the ground around their buildings, so cut back overgrowth and haul out debris before showings. A building permit is required before any demolition, so a seller who wants to remove a damaged garage or shed should apply first.

Clearing out a home is part of many sales. A residential garage sale needs a $10 permit from the City Clerk's Office, which asks for a state ID or driver's license showing the sale address.

sections.h2: Forms for the Oak Park assessor
sections.html:
The Assessor's Office is at 14000 Oak Park Boulevard. Two filings follow a sale.

  • Property Transfer Affidavit: needed whenever ownership changes, including title, beneficial use or ownership interest, with a 45-day deadline from the transfer.
  • Request to Rescind Principal Residence Exemption: filed by homeowners who sell or convert their principal residence so the exemption ends.

The buyer files a new exemption form after closing, listed by the city as Form 2368, at the same counter. Ask your closing agent which of these it handles so none is filed twice or skipped.

The deed goes to the Oakland County Register of Deeds. County transfer tax is 55 cents for each $500 of consideration and state tax is $3.75 for each $500. Consideration under $100.00 is exempt, and the reason for any exemption has to be written on the face of the document.

The office asks for notarized signatures, a 2-1/2 inch blank top margin, and an embossed seal on any death certificate filed. Its index reaches back to January 1, 1964, so you can pull your own earlier deed and confirm the legal description before signing. A warranty deed is first tax certified at the county treasurer's office for $5.00, and recording costs $30.00.

Once you accept an offer, the work splits into a few short tasks. First, the closing agent orders title work and checks that no lien or unpaid tax sits on the parcel. Second, you confirm with Municipal Services whether the house needs a certificate of occupancy or a rental inspection, since a buyer cannot move in until those are settled. Third, the deed is prepared with notarized signatures and the correct margins so the county does not reject it.

After closing, the paperwork keeps moving. The deed is recorded at the county, the Property Transfer Affidavit goes to the assessor within 45 days, and you file the request to rescind your principal residence exemption. The buyer files a new exemption form. If you ran an alarm system, hand the permit information to the buyer.

sections.h2: What to bring when you call the city
sections.html:
Have your parcel number and street address ready before you phone Municipal Services or the Assessor's Office. Ask what is on record for permits, whether a certificate of occupancy applies, and whether a rental registration is still active for the house. Write down the name of the department and the date you called so your closing agent can follow up.

For a house that was rented, bring the lease dates and the last inspection record. For a house with a garage or shed you plan to remove, ask about the demolition permit before any work starts. These calls take a few minutes and usually save a delay at closing.

faqs.q: Is an inspection required before an Oak Park house is sold?
faqs.a: The city requires a certificate of occupancy for new or altered buildings and a rental inspection every two years or after a change in tenancy. Ask Municipal Services whether your house, particularly one that has been rented, needs either before a buyer moves in.

faqs.q: What does a certificate of occupancy cost in Oak Park?
faqs.a: The fee schedule prints $50 for occupancy only and $50 for reissuance. Commercial and renovation certificates carry different amounts.

faqs.q: Should an Oak Park seller do anything about the alarm permit?
faqs.a: The city charges a one-time $20 fee and requires a new permit each time an operable alarm changes owners. Tell the buyer so they register the system in their own name.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for the Property Transfer Affidavit in Oak Park?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the transfer, filed at the Assessor's Office, 14000 Oak Park Boulevard. It covers any change in title, beneficial use or ownership interest.

faqs.q: Where does the deed for an Oak Park house get filed?
faqs.a: At the Oakland County Register of Deeds. A warranty deed is first tax certified at the county treasurer's office for $5.00, and recording costs $30.00.
